behavior: observeNextAction reads every goal (parents, dependencies, deadline, health, order, score, latest progress, last activation including a resume) and each goal's latest settled result however old (a check, or the item closed in Tasks). It reads open work (accepted and not settled, or proposed today and not decided; at most 500, newest first, the rest counted), open commitments that are not work items, titles of commitments finished in the last 30 days, the readiness of each workflow version open work runs, and for a waiting run who resumes it (its own timer, an outside call to a webhook step, or you). It writes nothing.

planNextAction is a pure function of that snapshot. Candidates rank in a stated order: check a finished result, resolve a blocker, restore what accepted work needs, decide a proposal from today, continue accepted work, record whether a goal that looks done is done, start an unblocked goal step, review a goal; within a kind by the soonest deadline and worst health on the goal or any parent, then goal order from the top goal down, then age. The rationale names the field that decided.

Doing nothing new is always weighed; it wins when open items (open work plus plain commitments due by the end of today) reach capacity (default 5) and every option adds work, or when nothing achievable remains.

Guards: no work or step behind an inactive goal or parent or an unfinished dependency of the goal or any parent (a parent waiting on its own step does not hold it); dependencies that can never finish ask for a fix; timer and outside-webhook waits are not offered; no step duplicating an open commitment or work item (titles compared ignoring case and punctuation); a task whose latest settled work passed, a goal whose steps are all complete, a goal with score 1.0 or one whose exact title was finished as a commitment gets a prompt to record whether it is done, and its proposals are held back; stale goals (14 days without progress, activation, settled result or accepted work, or escalation suggesting a stop) get a review prompt and their proposals are held back; checking and settling failed or missing runs continue under a held goal.

It asks instead of guessing when a goal above task level has no next concrete step, when a task's last attempt failed, or when two goals' new steps have nothing (deadline, health, order) between them; a tie never replaces a question of the goal's own.

Each result carries the goal and its read revision, the goal path, evidence references, a rationale against doing nothing and the runner-up, the work item to link or null, an expiry (12 hours or the soonest deadline on the goal or a parent) and a basis digest of every input except the clock, which run progress does not change. considered lists up to 20 alternatives, exclusions first, and omitted counts what was cut. Dates in messages use the user's time zone, and quoted outside text (blocker reasons, check summaries) is clipped to 200 characters.

limitations: Signals are structured only: goals, work items, commitments, checked results and workflow readiness. Calendar, mail and facts are not read.
New steps come from the user's own goal titles; a missing step is asked for, never invented.
Plain commitments guard against duplicates and fill the day only when due by its end; they are not recommended. F-13 links work items.
Duplicates and finished commitments are matched on normalized titles; a reworded one is not caught.
Recurring work is not modeled: a task whose work passed looks done until the user accepts new work for it or closes it.
A wait the planner cannot attribute is treated as the user's, because hiding an approval would stall the work.
The ranking is a stated preference order, not a measured optimum; the scenarios and rubric await founder review.
found: The morning plan reads active and overdue goals and yesterday's review summary, but not dependencies, open work or checked results. It never deduplicates against existing commitments and writes its actions straight into work items. Q-18 does not change it; F-13 decides whether What's next? replaces it.

Deciding or rejecting a work item never changes its commitment's status, and the upgrade turned every historical morning-plan action into a pending proposal. Readers of open commitments must filter on the work decision, as the Today view and this planner do.

Tasks and the commitments tool change a work item's commitment status directly, outside the work-item API. Approval links resume through a webhook, like outside calls; only the waiting step's piece tells them apart.

review.result: An independent code review found 5 blocking and 16 smaller issues and asked 3 questions. All are fixed in 45cc2d32; 9a298152 adds the #573 reader review the fixes required and clips quoted outside text. Each guarantee has a test that fails when it is removed (51 of 51).
blocking: 1: rejected and undecided proposals stayed open forever, read oldest first under a 500-row cap, so they crowded out new work and filled the day
2: proposals skipped the dependency, done and stale guards and hid their goal's review
3: dependencies were not inherited from parents, so a task under a milestone waiting on another was offered as startable
4: work checked done was forgotten after 7 days, done work without a goal link was never seen, and the done review ranked below every new step
5: timer and outside-webhook waits were offered as blockers to answer
minor: status changes made in Tasks were ignored, and the missing-run advice could not be carried out (6)
an answer under a paused goal was still pushed (7)
parents' deadlines and in-between goal order were ignored (8)
the rationale blamed deadline, health or order when age or title decided (9)
a full day hid options that add no work (10)
dependencies that can never finish held a goal silently (11)
a goal activated or resumed recently was called stale (12)
the write check counted rows, and observer paths had no live tests (14)
the doc claimed every goal and every alternative, and the receipt marked the blocked-work check passed (15)
the receipts named a local tool path; fixed here and on Q-01, Q-02 and Q-13 (16)
nits: wording for restoring a capability, a tie replacing a question, no evidence for a full day of commitments, UTC dates, scenario wording (17 to 21)
questions: Q1: F-13 compares basis, not the goal revision, which is a read projection that health and escalation updates also change
Q2: run progress no longer changes the basis; a run starting, pausing or finishing does
Q3: F-13 can keep a tie's answer as goal order with the existing reorderGoals, which the planner reads
